Key findings

What this sample shows

These observations describe qualified ScreenSize.net sessions during the reporting period. They are not global device or browser market-share estimates.

  1. /01

    Common desktop pair

    1920 × 920 CSS pixels is the most common desktop pair, representing 11.7% of qualified desktop observations.

  2. /02

    The height checkpoint

    The desktop median page viewport height is 920px in this observed sample. Use the calculator to test a hero or CTA against the full distribution.

  3. /03

    Mobile width concentration

    The mobile median viewport width is 400px. Narrower and wider buckets remain visible in the cumulative distribution.

Sampling Governance

Legacy tablet observations are excluded because the original classifier could mistake touch-enabled desktop computers for tablets.

Clear dimension anomalies are excluded from published rankings but remain in aggregate storage for auditing.

Observed viewport proportions

Each point is a rounded aggregate bucket. Larger points represent more qualified observations within that environment.

Methodology

How to read this report

This report describes ScreenSize.net browser observations, not global device or browser market share.

Collection and privacy

A browser tab contributes at most one sample during its session. Measurements are rounded into monthly aggregate buckets. No IP addresses, user IDs, precise timestamps or full user-agent strings are stored. Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track signals are honored.

Quality and limitations

Viewports wider than 6,000 CSS pixels or taller than 4,000 are excluded from published distributions. Historical DPR values are normalized to 0.05 steps. Device class is inferred locally and remains an approximation. Width and height quantiles are marginal summaries and may not describe one paired viewport.

How to read this report

This report describes ScreenSize.net browser observations, not global device or browser market share.

Collection and privacy

A browser tab contributes at most one sample during its session. Measurements are rounded into monthly aggregate buckets. No IP addresses, user IDs, precise timestamps or full user-agent strings are stored. Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track signals are honored.

Quality and limitations

Viewports wider than 6,000 CSS pixels or taller than 4,000 are excluded from published distributions. Historical DPR values are normalized to 0.05 steps. Device class is inferred locally and remains an approximation. Width and height quantiles are marginal summaries and may not describe one paired viewport.
